title: In Darkness as in Light
description: In Darkness as in Light in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 129 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"The darkness and the light are both alike to thee."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In dark-ness as in light, Hid-den a-like from view, I sleep, I wake with-in His sight, Who looks ex-is-tence through.

lines: I sleep, I wake within His sight,
From the dim hour of birth,
All that I am, — have been, —
All that I yet may be,
He sees at once, as he hath seen,

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
